results.name: parity_outlier_neighbour_yes
results.description: In sets of >= 3 examples where exactly one example differs in parity from all others, yes rate for non-example targets within 3 of that off-parity example; observed > null means people generalise around the exception (treat it as an interval seed) more than the rule-plus-exception model, observed < null means they reject its neighbours more firmly.
results.code:
# name: parity_outlier_neighbour_yes
# description: In sets of >= 3 examples where exactly one example differs in parity from all others, yes rate for non-example targets within 3 of that off-parity example; observed > null means people generalise around the exception (treat it as an interval seed) more than the rule-plus-exception model, observed < null means they reject its neighbours more firmly.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    nonex = dist > 0
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    odd = np.where(np.isnan(ex), np.nan, ex % 2)
    n_odd = np.nansum(odd, axis=1)
    lone_odd = (n >= 3) & (n_odd == 1)
    lone_even = (n >= 3) & (n_odd == n - 1)
    want = np.where(lone_odd, 1.0, np.where(lone_even, 0.0, -1.0))
    is_out = (odd == want[:, None])
    d_out = np.nanmin(np.where(is_out, np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), np.nan), axis=1) if is_out.any() else np.full(len(t), np.nan)
    m = (lone_odd | lone_even) & nonex & (np.nan_to_num(d_out, nan=99.0) <= 3)
    return rate(m)

results.name: near_minus_mid_distance_gradient
results.description: For sets of >= 2 examples, yes rate for non-example targets 1-2 from the nearest example minus those 6-15 away; observed > null means people's similarity gradient falls off more steeply than the model's interval mixture, observed < null means flatter.
results.code:

# description: For sets of >= 2 examples, yes rate for non-example targets 1-2 from the nearest example minus those 6-15 away; observed > null means people's similarity gradient falls off more steeply than the model's interval mixture, observed < null means flatter.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    nonex = dist > 0
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    return rate((n >= 2) & nonex & (dist <= 2)) - rate((n >= 2) & (dist >= 6) & (dist <= 15))

results.name: round_number_target_yes
results.description: Yes rate for targets that are multiples of 10 on sets containing no multiple-of-10 example and with the target 3+ from every example; observed > null means people endorse round numbers as a salient default beyond the model, observed < null less.
results.code:
# name: round_number_target_yes
# description: Yes rate for targets that are multiples of 10 on sets containing no multiple-of-10 example and with the target 3+ from every example; observed > null means people endorse round numbers as a salient default beyond the model, observed < null less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    nonex = dist > 0
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    ex10 = np.any(np.nan_to_num(ex, nan=1.0) % 10 == 0, axis=1)
    return rate((t % 10 == 0) & ~ex10 & (dist >= 3))

results.name: odd_set_prime_minus_nonprime_yes
results.description: Among sets of >= 2 examples that are all odd, yes rate for odd prime non-example targets minus odd non-prime non-example targets; observed > null means people pick up primality more than the model, observed < null means the model overweights the primes rule relative to people.
results.code:
# name: odd_set_prime_minus_nonprime_yes
# description: Among sets of >= 2 examples that are all odd, yes rate for odd prime non-example targets minus odd non-prime non-example targets; observed > null means people pick up primality more than the model, observed < null means the model overweights the primes rule relative to people.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    nonex = dist > 0
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    odd_set = (n >= 2) & (np.nansum(np.where(np.isnan(ex), 0, ex % 2), axis=1) == n)
    ti = t.astype(int)
    primes = np.array([k > 1 and all(k % a for a in range(2, int(k ** 0.5) + 1)) for k in range(101)])
    pr = primes[ti]
    todd = ti % 2 == 1
    return rate(odd_set & nonex & todd & pr) - rate(odd_set & nonex & todd & ~pr)

results.name: digit_reversal_target_yes
results.description: Yes rate for targets that are the digit reversal of a two-digit example (e.g. 38 for 83, non-palindromic, target not itself an example); observed > null means people use a digit-reversal / shared-digits concept the model lacks, observed < null less.
results.code:
# name: digit_reversal_target_yes
# description: Yes rate for targets that are the digit reversal of a two-digit example (e.g. 38 for 83, non-palindromic, target not itself an example); observed > null means people use a digit-reversal / shared-digits concept the model lacks, observed < null less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    nonex = dist > 0
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    exn = np.nan_to_num(ex, nan=0.0)
    rev = (exn % 10) * 10 + np.floor(exn / 10)
    ok = (exn >= 10) & (exn <= 99) & (exn % 10 != 0) & (rev != exn)
    hit = np.any(ok & (rev == t[:, None]), axis=1)
    return rate(hit & nonex)

results.name: far_high_minus_low_target_yes
results.description: Among targets more than 10 from every example, yes rate for targets >= 70 minus targets <= 30; observed > null means people favour large numbers (or the model over-favours small ones via its compressed number line), observed < null the reverse.

results.name: same_decade_nonneighbour_yes
results.description: For sets of >= 2 examples, yes rate for non-example targets sharing the tens digit (floor(t/10), 100 counted as 10) with some example but 3+ away from every example; observed > null means people use a same-decade concept the model lacks, observed < null means the model over-generalises within decades.
results.code:
# name: same_decade_nonneighbour_yes
# description: For sets of >= 2 examples, yes rate for non-example targets sharing the tens digit (floor(t/10), 100 counted as 10) with some example but 3+ away from every example; observed > null means people use a same-decade concept the model lacks, observed < null means the model over-generalises within decades.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float).values
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).values
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    nonex = dist > 0
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    dec = np.floor(np.minimum(t, 99) / 10)
    exdec = np.floor(np.minimum(ex, 99) / 10)
    same = np.any(exdec == dec[:, None], axis=1)
    return rate((n >= 2) & same & (dist >= 3))
